units.en: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you will weigh it yourself.
units.literal: The logic of fortune and calamity — I think you will weigh it yourself.

units.zh: 論曰：文襄嗣膺霸道，威略昭著。
units.en: The appraisal says: Wenxiang inherited the hegemonic enterprise, and his power and strategy were unmistakable.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Wenxiang succeeded to the hegemonic enterprise, and his martial strategy was plainly displayed.

units.zh: 而志在峻法，急於禦下，於前王之德，有所未同。
units.en: Yet he set his mind on harsh law and was impatient in ruling those below him; in this he fell short of the former king's virtue.
units.literal: Yet his intent lay in severe laws and he was harsh in governing subordinates; in the virtue of the former king, there was something with which he did not accord.

units.zh: 生而岐嶷，神武異之。
units.en: From birth he was precocious and keen; Gao Huan took him for a prodigy.
units.literal: From birth he was precocious and sharp; Shenwu regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 武定四年十一月，神武西討，不豫班師，文襄馳赴軍所，侍衛還晉陽。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Wuding 4 (546), Gao Huan marched west, fell ill, and withdrew; Gao Cheng raced to the army, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding, Shenwu campaigned west and, falling ill, withdrew the army; Wenxiang raced to the army's camp, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.

units.zh: 五年正月丙午，神武崩，秘不發喪。
units.en: In the first month of Wuding 5 (547), on bingwu day, Gao Huan died; the death was kept secret.
units.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on bingwu, Shenwu died; the death was kept secret.

units.zh: 夏四月壬申，文襄朝於鄴。
units.en: In the fourth month, on renshen day, Gao Cheng attended court at Ye.
units.literal: In the fourth month, on renshen, Wenxiang attended court at Ye.

units.zh: 秘不發喪，徐出言曰：「奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。」
units.en: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced, "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."
units.literal: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced: "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."

units.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱捨，於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。
units.en: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
units.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

units.zh: 遣司空韓軌率衆討之。
units.en: Gao Cheng sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.
units.literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.

units.zh: 丁丑，文襄還晉陽，乃發喪，告喻文武，陳神武遺志。
units.en: On dingchou day Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang, announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Gao Huan's final wishes.
units.literal: On dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Shenwu's final wishes.

units.zh: 文襄啟辭位，願停王爵。
units.en: Gao Cheng memorialized to decline and wished to relinquish the princely rank.
units.literal: Wenxiang memorialized to decline the post and wished to relinquish the princely rank.

units.zh: 八月戊辰，文襄啟申神武遺令，請減國邑分封將督，各有差。
units.en: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Gao Cheng memorialized to carry out Gao Huan's final command, asking to reduce the royal fief and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Wenxiang memorialized to carry out Shenwu's final command, asking to reduce the fiefs of the realm and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.

units.zh: 王尋覽書，問誰為作。
units.en: When Gao Cheng had read the letter, he asked who had written it.
units.literal: When the Prince had read the letter, he asked who had written it.

units.zh: 王曰：「偉才如此，何因不使我知？」
units.en: Gao Cheng said, "With talent like this, why was I not told?"
units.literal: The Prince said: "With talent like this, why was I not told?"

units.zh: 王欲間景於梁，又與景書而謬其辭，云本使景陽叛，欲與圖西，西人知之，故景更與圖南為事。
units.en: Gao Cheng wished to drive a wedge between Hou Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally sent Jing to stir rebellion at Jingyang and meant to plot the west together; when Western Wei learned of it, Jing turned instead to plotting with the south.
units.literal: The Prince wished to drive a wedge between Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally had Jing stir rebellion at Jingyang and planned with him to strike west; when Western Wei learned this, Jing turned instead to scheming with the south.

units.zh: 壬申，東魏主與王獵於鄴東，馳逐如飛。
units.en: On renshen the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with Gao Cheng east of Ye, galloping as if in flight.
units.literal: On renshen, the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with the Prince east of Ye, racing as if flying.

units.zh: 監衛都督烏那羅受工伐從後呼曰：「天子莫走馬，大將軍怒。」
units.en: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind, "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"
units.literal: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind: "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"

units.zh: 王怒曰：「朕！
units.en: Gao Cheng raged, "Imperial We!
units.literal: The Prince raged: "Imperial We!

units.zh: 東魏主賜季舒彩，季舒未敢即受，啟之於王，王使取一段。
units.en: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to Gao Cheng, who told him to take one bolt.
units.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to the Prince, who told him to take one bolt.

units.zh: 三月辛亥，王南臨黎陽，濟於虎牢，自洛陽從太行而反晉陽。
units.en: On xinhai of the third month Gao Cheng went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang from Luoyang by way of the Taihang.
units.literal: On xinhai of the third month, the Prince went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang by way of Taihang from Luoyang.

units.zh: 六月，王巡北邊城戍，賑賜有差。
units.en: In the sixth month Gao Cheng toured the northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.
units.literal: In the sixth month the Prince toured northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.

units.zh: 七月，王還晉陽。
units.en: In the seventh month Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang.
units.literal: In the seventh month the Prince returned to Jinyang.

units.zh: 識者以為王將殂之兆也。
units.en: Those who understood took it as an omen that Gao Cheng would die.
units.literal: Those who understood took it as an omen that the Prince would die.

units.zh: 初，梁將蘭欽子京為東魏所虜，王命以配廚。
units.en: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of the Liang general Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; Gao Cheng ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.
units.literal: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of Liang General Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; the Prince ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.

units.zh: 欽請贖之，王不許。
units.en: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; Gao Cheng refused.
units.literal: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; the Prince refused.

units.zh: 京再訴，王使監廚蒼頭薛豐洛杖之，曰：「更訴當殺爾。」
units.en: Jing appealed again; Gao Cheng had the kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said, "Complain again and you will be killed."
units.literal: Jing appealed again; the Prince had kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said: "Complain again and you will be killed."

units.zh: 王曰：「小人新杖之，故嚇我耳。」
units.en: Gao Cheng said, "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."
units.literal: The Prince said: "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."

units.zh: 京將進食，王却，謂諸人曰：「昨夜夢此奴斫我，宜殺却。」
units.en: When Jing was about to bring food, Gao Cheng held back and told the others, "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."
units.literal: When Jing was about to bring food, the Prince held back and told the others: "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."

units.zh: 王怒曰：「我未索食，爾何據來！」
units.en: Gao Cheng raged, "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"
units.literal: The Prince raged: "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"

units.zh: 王自投傷足，入于床下。
units.en: Gao Cheng threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.
units.literal: The Prince threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.

units.zh: 然文襄之禍生所忽，蓋有由焉。
units.en: Yet Wenxiang's disaster grew out of what he neglected; it had its cause.
units.literal: Yet Wenxiang's disaster arose from what he neglected; there was surely a cause for it.

units.zh: 令楊愔傳旨，謂國子助教許散愁曰：「先生在世何以自資？」
units.en: He had Yang Yin deliver his message to Xu Sanchou, assistant instructor at the National University: "Sir, how do you occupy yourself in this life?"
units.literal: He had Yang Yin convey the imperial message and say to National University assistant instructor Xu Sanchou, "Sir, in this life by what do you support yourself?"

units.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。
units.en: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

units.zh: 及承大位，楊愔、燕子獻、宋欽道等同輔。
units.en: When he came to the throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others served jointly as his advisers.
units.literal: When he inherited the great throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others assisted him together.

units.zh: 以常山王地親望重，內外畏服，加以文宣初崩之日，太后本欲立之，故愔等並懷猜忌。
units.en: Prince Yan of Changshan was a close kinsman with formidable prestige, feared and obeyed at court and beyond. Since the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him when Emperor Wenxuan died, Yang Yin and the others all suspected him.
units.literal: Because the Prince of Changshan was close in kinship and weighty in reputation, and those within and without feared and submitted to him, and because on the day Emperor Wenxuan first died the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him, Yin and the others all harbored suspicion.

units.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。
units.en: His chief ministers may have been sincere, but they could not help him enlarge the Way and virtue or keep harmony among his kin. Nor could they plan far enough to protect themselves or safeguard their lord. When decision was needed they failed to decide, and brought disaster on themselves.
units.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, although they held sincere intentions, could neither assist him in magnifying the Way and virtue and harmonizing his close kin, nor plan farsightedly to protect themselves and deeply scheme to safeguard their lord; when they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought blame upon themselves.

units.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。
units.en: The ministers were exterminated, and the ruler, though still alive, was deposed and humiliated. All of it came from entrusting affairs to men unequal to the task.
units.literal: The ministers were already executed and wiped out, while the ruler, though alive, was deposed and humiliated; all this came from entrusting office to men who were not equal to the task.

units.zh: 時太原公洋在城東雙堂，入而討賊，臠割京等，皆漆其頭。
units.en: At the time Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
units.literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

units.zh: 及西魏將獨孤信入洛，署為開府記室。
units.en: When Western Wei general Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he appointed Xi recorder on his opening staff.
units.literal: When Western Wei general Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he appointed Xi recorder on his opening staff.

units.zh: 俄而信返，晞遂歸鄴。
units.en: Soon Dugu Xin returned west; Xi then went back to Ye.
units.literal: Soon Dugu Xin returned west; Xi then went back to Ye.

units.zh: 孝昭皇帝演，字延安，神武皇帝第六子，文宣皇帝之母弟也。
units.en: Emperor Xiaozhao, whose personal name was Yan and style name Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan by the same mother.

units.zh: 大寧元年閏十二月癸卯，梓宮還鄴，上諡曰孝昭皇帝。
units.en: In the intercalary twelfth month of Daning 1, on guimao, his coffin was returned to Ye, and he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao.
units.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the first year of Daning, on guimao, the imperial coffin returned to Ye, and the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao was presented.

units.zh: 魏元象元年，封常山郡公。
units.en: In the first year of the Yuanxiang era of Wei, he was made Duke of Changshan Commandery.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang of Wei, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.

units.zh: 唯常山王至，內外肅然。
units.en: Only when the Prince of Changshan appeared did the palace fall silent and straighten itself.
units.literal: Only when the Prince of Changshan arrived would inside and outside become solemn and awestruck.

units.zh: 皇建元年八月壬午，皇帝即位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，改乾明元年為皇建。
units.en: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the first year of Huangjian, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming to Huangjian.
units.literal: On the renwu day of the eighth month of Huangjian year 1, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming year 1 to Huangjian.

units.zh: 五年，除幷省尚書令。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat for the combined provinces.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat of the Joint Provinces.

units.zh: 八年，轉司空、錄尚書事。
units.en: In the eighth year he was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Minister of Works and made Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 帝長於政術，剖斷咸盡其理，文宣歎重之。
units.en: The prince had a gift for statecraft; every ruling he handed down went to the heart of the matter, and Emperor Wenxuan marveled at him.
units.literal: The Emperor excelled in the art of governance; his analyses and judgments all exhaustively addressed the principles involved, and Wenxuan sighed in admiration and held him in high esteem.

units.zh: 幼而英特，早有大成之量，武明皇太后早所愛重。
units.en: Even as a boy he was remarkable, showing early promise of greatness, and Empress Dowager Wuming had cherished him from the start.
units.literal: From childhood he was outstanding; early on he showed the measure of great accomplishment, and Empress Dowager Wuming had loved and esteemed him from the first.

units.zh: 及文襄執政，遣中書侍郎李同軌就霸府為諸弟師。
units.en: Once Wenxiang took charge of the government, he dispatched Li Tonggui, Gentleman of the Secretariat, to the Overlord's residence to instruct his younger brothers.
units.literal: When Wenxiang came to hold power, he sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui to the Overlord's residence to serve as tutor to the younger brothers.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 順成后本魏朝宗室，文宣欲帝離之，陰為帝廣求淑媛，望移其寵。
units.en: Empress Shuncheng came from the Wei imperial clan. Emperor Wenxuan wanted the prince to turn from her and secretly searched out worthy beauties for him, hoping to draw his heart elsewhere.
units.literal: Empress Shuncheng was originally of the imperial clan of Wei; Wenxuan wanted the Emperor to distance himself from her, and secretly sought fine ladies widely for the Emperor, hoping to shift his favor.

units.zh: 冬十一月辛亥，立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為皇太子。
units.en: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Gao Bainian as crown prince.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on the xinhai day, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Bainian as crown prince.

units.zh: 豈幽顯之間，實有報復，將齊之基宇止在於斯，帝欲大之，天不許也？
units.en: Was there retribution at work between the seen and unseen worlds—and was the Northern Qi destined to rise no higher? He sought to expand its domain, but Heaven would not allow it.
units.literal: Was it that between the hidden and the manifest there is truly retribution, and that the foundation of Qi would extend no further—he wished to enlarge it, but Heaven would not permit it?

units.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。
units.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, he was raised to princely rank.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his rank was advanced to prince.

units.zh: 九年，除大司馬，仍錄尚書。
units.en: In the ninth year he was made Grand Marshal while retaining his post as Recorder of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Grand Marshal, while still serving as Recorder of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 及文宣崩，帝居禁中護喪事，幼主即位，乃即朝班。
units.en: When Emperor Wenxuan died, Xiaozhao remained in the palace to oversee the funeral. Once the young ruler took the throne, he entered the court ranks.
units.literal: When Wenxuan died, the emperor remained inside the palace to oversee the funeral arrangements; after the young ruler ascended the throne, he then took his place in the court ranks.

units.zh: 除太傅、錄尚書，朝政皆決於帝。
units.en: He was appointed grand tutor and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court affairs were decided by him.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court government was decided by the emperor.

units.zh: 時楊愔、燕子獻、可朱渾天和、宋欽道、鄭子默等以帝威望旣重，內懼權逼，請以帝為太師、司州牧、錄尚書事；
units.en: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and the others saw how great his prestige had become and secretly feared the pressure of his authority. They asked that he be made grand preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and recorder of the Masters of Writing;
units.literal: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and others, because the emperor’s prestige had become weighty and they inwardly feared the pressure of his power, requested that he be made Grand Preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;

units.zh: 詔以帝為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，相府佐史進位一等。
units.en: An edict appointed him Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and all staff of the chancellery were promoted one rank.
units.literal: An edict appointed the Emperor Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; assistants and clerks of the chancellery were promoted one rank.

units.zh: 先是帝不豫而無闕聽覽，是月，崩於晉陽宮，時年二十七。
units.en: Before this the emperor had been ill, yet he had not neglected audiences or reviews of affairs. That month he died in Jinyang Palace at the age of twenty-seven.
units.literal: Before this, the emperor had been ill but had not neglected hearings and review; that month he died in Jinyang Palace, aged twenty-seven.

units.zh: 庚午，葬於文靖陵。
units.en: On gengwu he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.
units.literal: On gengwu, he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.

units.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，儀望風表，迥然獨秀。
units.en: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and presence he stood apart, towering above all others.
units.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and appearance he stood alone, towering above others.

units.zh: 帝聰敏有識度，深沉能斷，不可窺測。
units.en: The emperor was quick-witted and far-sighted, deep and decisive—his inner thoughts could not be read.
units.literal: The emperor was keen and perceptive, with breadth of judgment; deep and resolute, he could not be fathomed.

units.zh: 澤率爾對曰：「陛下聰明至公，自可遠侔古昔，而有識之士，咸言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。」
units.en: Pei Ze answered without hesitation: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the sages of antiquity, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters—the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."
units.literal: Ze answered straight off: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the ancients of old, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters; the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."

units.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可。
units.en: The prince secretly drew up a list of grievances and prepared to remonstrate, but his friend Wang Xi urged him not to.
units.literal: The Emperor also secretly drafted a list of matters and was about to remonstrate; his friend Wang Xi thought it inadvisable.

units.zh: 先是禁友王晞，乃捨之，令侍帝。
units.en: Wang Xi, his friend, had earlier been placed under restriction; now Emperor Wenxuan freed him and set him to wait on the prince.
units.literal: Earlier Wang Xi, his friend, had been confined; now he released him and ordered him to attend the Emperor.

units.zh: 同軌病卒，又命開府長流參軍刁柔代之，性嚴褊，不適誘訓之宜，中被遣出。
units.en: After Tonggui died of illness, Diao Rou, a senior staff officer in the chief's office, was appointed in his place—but Diao was harsh and rigid, ill suited to teaching, and before long was dismissed.
units.literal: When Tonggui died of illness, he again ordered Diao Rou, Staff Supervisor of the Chief's Office, to replace him; Diao's nature was stern and narrow, unsuited to guidance and instruction, and midway through he was dismissed and sent away.

units.zh: 遂篤志讀《漢書》，至《李陵傳》，恒壯其所為焉。
units.en: He then applied himself to the Book of Han; when he came to the biography of Li Ling, he always took fierce pride in Li Ling's conduct.
units.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to reading the Book of Han, and when he reached the "Biography of Li Ling," he always admired what Li Ling had done.

units.zh: 七年，從文宣還鄴。
units.en: In the seventh year he returned to Ye with Emperor Wenxuan.
units.literal: In the seventh year, he followed Wenxuan back to Ye.

units.zh: 乾明元年，從廢帝赴鄴，居於領軍府。
units.en: In Qianming 1 he accompanied Emperor Fei to Ye and resided at the headquarters of the Commanding General.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianming, he followed Emperor Fei to Ye and lived at the headquarters of the Commanding General.

units.zh: 三月甲戌，帝初上省，旦發領軍府，大風暴起，壞所御車幔，帝甚惡之。
units.en: On the jiaxu day of the third month, the prince went to the Secretariat for the first time. At dawn he left the Commander-in-Chief's headquarters; a sudden gale tore the curtains of his carriage, and he took it as a dire omen.
units.literal: On the jiaxu day of the third month, the Emperor for the first time went to the Secretariat; at dawn he set out from the Commander-in-Chief's office; a violent windstorm arose and destroyed the curtains of his carriage—the Emperor regarded it as highly ominous.

units.zh: 二年春正月辛亥，祀圓丘。
units.en: On the xinhai day of the first month of the second year, he sacrificed at the Altar of Heaven.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of year 2, on the xinhai day, he sacrificed at the Round Altar.

units.zh: 十一月甲辰，詔曰：「朕嬰此暴疾，奄忽無逮。
units.en: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict declared, "I have been struck by a sudden grave illness and can no longer attend to affairs.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict said: "I have been stricken by this violent illness and suddenly can no longer reach affairs.

units.zh: 是月，帝親戎北討庫莫奚，出長城，虜奔遁，分兵致討，大獲牛馬，括總入晉陽宮。
units.en: That month the emperor personally led a campaign north against the Kumo Xi. He passed beyond the Great Wall; the enemy fled in rout; he sent columns in pursuit and captured large herds of cattle and horses, which were tallied and brought into Jinyang Palace.
units.literal: That month, the emperor personally took the field and marched north to attack the Kumo Xi; he passed beyond the Great Wall, the enemy fled in rout, he sent troops in separate columns to pursue them, captured large numbers of cattle and horses, and tallied the whole and brought it into Jinyang Palace.

units.zh: 坐定，酒數行，執尚書令楊愔、右僕射燕子獻、領軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道等於坐。
units.en: They had barely settled in and taken a few cups when he seized Chief Minister Yang Yin, Right Vice Director Yanzi Xian, Commander-in-Chief Kezhuhun Tianhe, Palace Attendant Song Qindao, and the rest where they sat.
units.literal: Once seated, after a few rounds of wine, he seized Chief Minister Yang Yin, Right Deputy Director Yanzi Xian, Commander-in-Chief Kezhuhun Tianhe, Palace Attendant Song Qindao, and others at the banquet.

units.zh: 帝戎服與平原王段韶、平秦王高歸彥、領軍劉洪徽入自雲龍門，於中書省前遇散騎常侍鄭子默，又執之，同斬於御府之內。
units.en: In armor, with Prince Duan Shao of Pingyuan, Prince Gao Guiyan of Pingqin, and Commander-in-Chief Liu Honghui, he entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate. Before the Secretariat he met Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo, seized him too, and had them all beheaded inside the Imperial Treasury.
units.literal: The Emperor, in military garb, together with Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao, Prince of Pingqin Gao Guiyan, and Commander-in-Chief Liu Honghui, entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate; before the Secretariat they encountered Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo, seized him as well, and beheaded them all together inside the Imperial Treasury.

units.zh: 帝常恐濟南復興，乃密行鳩毒，濟南不從，乃扼而殺之。
units.en: The emperor, fearing that the Prince of Jinan might regain power, secretly sent poison; when the prince refused to take it, he was strangled to death.
units.literal: The Emperor often feared the Prince of Jinan would rise again, and so secretly administered poison; when the Prince of Jinan refused, he strangled him to death.

units.zh: 有兔驚馬，帝墜而絕肋。
units.en: A rabbit startled his horse, and the emperor fell, breaking his ribs.
units.literal: A rabbit startled the horse; the Emperor fell and broke his ribs.

units.zh: 每歎云：「雖盟津之師，左驂震而不衄。」
units.en: He often sighed and said, "Even when the army stood at Mengjin and the left outer horse shied, they did not break and flee."
units.literal: He would often sigh and say: "Even at the army at Mengjin, though the left outer horse was startled, they did not retreat in defeat."

units.zh: 帝笑曰：「誠如卿言。
units.en: The emperor smiled and said, "You are quite right.
units.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "It is truly as you say.

units.zh: 朕初臨萬機，慮不周悉，故致爾耳。
units.en: When I first assumed the throne, I had not yet grasped every detail of governance, and that is why this happened.
units.literal: When I first took charge of the myriad affairs of state, my concerns were not thorough and complete; that is why this came about.

units.zh: 此事安可久行，恐後又嫌疏漏。」
units.en: This cannot go on indefinitely—I am afraid you will later find me negligent again."
units.literal: How can this matter be carried on for long? I fear that afterward you will again find omissions.

units.zh: 趙郡王叡與厙狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「須拔我同堂弟，顯安我親姑子，今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。」
units.en: Prince of Zhao Gao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were seated in attendance. The emperor said, "Xu Ba is my cousin; Xian'an is my aunt's son. Today we observe family etiquette and put aside the formalities of ruler and subject—you may tell me where I fall short."
units.literal: Prince of Zhao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were in attendance seated beside him. The Emperor said: "Xu Ba is my paternal cousin; Xian'an is the son of my paternal aunt. Today let us observe family rites and set aside the respect due between ruler and minister—you may speak of where I fall short.

units.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「昔武王克殷，先封兩代，漢、魏、二晉，無廢茲典。
units.en: On the jiawu day, an edict stated: "When King Wu of Zhou conquered the Shang, he first enfeoffed descendants of the two preceding dynasties. The Han, Wei, and two Jin dynasties likewise never abandoned this precedent.
units.literal: On the jiawu day, an edict said: "In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Yin, he first enfeoffed the two former dynasties; Han, Wei, and the two Jin dynasties did not abandon this precedent.

units.zh: 及元氏統歷，不率舊章。
units.en: But when the Northern Wei held power, they ceased to follow the old rites.
units.literal: When the Yuan clan held the succession, they did not follow the old statutes.

units.zh: 朕纂承大業，思弘古典，但二王三恪，舊說不同，可議定是非，列名條奏。
units.en: We have inherited the imperial enterprise and wish to restore the ancient practice, but scholars disagree on the rites for enfeoffing descendants of prior dynasties; let the matter be debated, the correct view determined, and the names submitted in memorial.
units.literal: We have inherited the great enterprise and wish to restore the ancient model, but the old accounts differ on the two kings and three classes of former dynasties; the right and wrong should be debated and determined, and the names listed in a memorial.

units.zh: 其禮義體式亦仰議之。」
units.en: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should likewise be submitted for deliberation."
units.literal: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should also be submitted for deliberation."

units.zh: 今嗣子沖眇，未閑政術，社稷業重，理歸上德。
units.en: The heir is young and slight, not yet versed in statecraft. The charge of the dynasty is heavy, and by rights it should pass to one of highest virtue.
units.literal: Now the heir is young and slight, not yet practiced in the arts of government; the work of the altars of soil and grain is weighty, and by principle it returns to one of highest virtue.

units.zh: 其喪紀之禮一同漢文，三十六日悉從公除，山陵施用，務從儉約。」
units.en: As for mourning rites, follow entirely the precedent of Emperor Wen of Han. After thirty-six days all mourning shall be removed according to public rule, and the mausoleum expenses must be kept frugal."
units.literal: As for the rites of mourning, let all be the same as under Emperor Wen of Han; after thirty-six days, all shall follow public removal of mourning, and the expenditures for the mountain mausoleum must follow frugality."

units.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
units.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
units.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

units.zh: 初苦內熱，頻進湯散。
units.en: At first he was troubled by internal fever and took medicinal broths and powders repeatedly.
units.literal: At first he suffered from internal heat and frequently took decoctions and powders.

units.zh: 遂漸危篤。
units.en: His illness thereupon grew steadily worse.
units.literal: Thereupon his condition gradually became critical.

units.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
units.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
units.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

units.zh: 孝昭早居臺閤，故事通明，人吏之間，無所不委。
units.en: Emperor Xiaozhao had long served in the imperial secretariat, knew its precedents inside out, and was entrusted with every matter great and small.
units.literal: Xiaozhao early occupied the Terrace Pavilion; he was thoroughly versed in precedent; between men and officials nothing was not entrusted to him.
